state_meaning: AI-drafted candidate; no person has reviewed it.
text: The paper reports that when strongly incentivized to abstain when unsure, judges who read arguments are only slightly less likely to be confidently correct than those who do not, and also slightly less likely to be confidently wrong. A 2x2x2 repeated-measures ANOVA on the full 7-point scale shows a main effect of incentive structure (F(1,12)=13.2, p<0.01) and no other main effects or interactions; the authors take away that arguments are slightly harmful to accuracy when there is only a weak incentive to abstain (not statistically significant), a trend that disappears when judges need to be more sure before moving away from abstaining.
title: Arguments slightly but not significantly harmful under weak abstention incentives; trend disappears under strong ones
